title: Get Rid of Your Stuff
coreMove: Stuff is not silent: every kept object asks for space, care, money, and identity. Keep what serves real life, and let the rest stop owning you.

exampleSpecs.audience: professionals whose shelves are doing identity work
exampleSpecs.stakes: separate useful objects from display pressure
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: a peer uses Socrates in the Athens marketplace to reframe a stuck view of success objects

exampleSpecs.audience: learners who confuse simple living with copying an extreme
exampleSpecs.stakes: turn learner confusion into the working lesson
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: a teaching scene uses Diogenes, Cynicism, Athens, and the barrel tradition to clarify the non-imitation lesson

exampleSpecs.audience: readers who keep paying to move things they no longer use
exampleSpecs.stakes: show the same packing process before and after a restraint test
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: A packing pass changes when relief, not replacement cost, becomes the count.

exampleSpecs.audience: people whose possessions keep charging rent to identity
exampleSpecs.stakes: an object may survive because it protects an image, not a life
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: A peer uses Diogenes to reframe a storage fee as an identity charge.

exampleSpecs.audience: readers who argue with themselves while letting go
exampleSpecs.stakes: show wrong turns inside the mind before the clearer test appears
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: inner monologue uses Socrates, Athens, and marketplace restraint without external dialogue

exampleSpecs.audience: readers learning that objects keep making claims after purchase
exampleSpecs.stakes: simplicity may become a mood unless one visible claim is reduced
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: A close observation of one shelf carries the lesson without a planning frame.
